sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: Hi, Joanna, good to meet you.
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 嗨，乔安娜，很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Now, before we discuss your new research project, I'd like to hear something about the psychology study you did last year for your Master's degree.
sentences.zh: 现在，在讨论你的新研究项目之前，我想先了解一下你去年为硕士学位所开展的心理学研究。

sentences.en: So how did you choose your subjects for that?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是如何为那项研究选定受试者的呢？

sentences.en: JOANNA: Well. had six subjects, all professional musicians, and all female.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 嗯，我选了六位受试者，全部是职业音乐家，且均为女性。

sentences.en: Three were violinists and there was also a cello player and a pianist and a flute a player.
sentences.zh: 其中三位是小提琴演奏家，另有一位大提琴演奏家、一位钢琴演奏家和一位长笛演奏家。

sentences.en: They were all very highly regarded in the music world and they'd done quite extensive & 22 tours in different continents, and quite a few had won prizes and competitions as well.
sentences.zh: 她们在音乐界均享有极高声誉，曾在各大洲进行过相当广泛的巡演，其中不少人还赢得过各类奖项和比赛。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: And they were quite young, weren't they?
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 她们年纪都比较轻，对吧？

sentences.en: JOANNA: Yes, between 25 and 29 - the mean was 27.8.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 是的，年龄介于25至29岁之间——平均年龄为27.8岁。

sentences.en: I wasn't specifically looking for & 22 artists who'd produced recordings, but this is something that's just taken for granted these days, and they all had.
sentences.zh: 我并未特意挑选那些已发行过录音作品的艺术家，但如今这几乎已成为一种默认前提，而她们全都发行过录音作品。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: Right.
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 好的。

sentences.en: Now you collected your data through telephone interviews, didn't you?
sentences.zh: 你现在是通过电话访谈来收集数据的，对吗？

sentences.en: JOANNA: Yes. realised if I was going to interview leading musicians it'd only be possible. & 24 over the phone because they're so busy.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 是的。我意识到，若要采访顶尖音乐家，唯一可行的方式只能是电话访谈，因为她们实在太忙了。

sentences.en: I recorded them using a telephone recording adaptor.
sentences.zh: 我使用电话录音适配器对访谈进行了录音。

sentences.en: I'd been worried about the quality, but it worked out all right.
sentences.zh: 我原本还担心录音质量，但实际效果还不错。

sentences.en: I managed at least a 30-minute interview with each subject, sometimes longer.
sentences.zh: 我成功地对每位受试者完成了至少30分钟的访谈，有时甚至更长。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: Did doing it on the phone make it more stressful?
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 采用电话访谈的方式是否让整个过程压力更大？

sentences.en: JOANNA: I'd thought it might ... it was all quite informal though and in fact they seemed very keen to talk.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 我原本以为可能会……不过整个访谈氛围其实非常轻松随意，事实上，她们似乎都非常乐于交谈。

sentences.en: And I don't think using the phone meant I got less rich data. & 24 rather the opposite in fact.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，使用电话访谈并未导致我获取的数据深度降低；恰恰相反，实际情况可能正相反。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: Interesting.
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 很有意思。

sentences.en: And you were looking at how performers dress for concert performances?
sentences.zh: 你当时的研究焦点是表演者在音乐会演出时的着装方式，对吗？

sentences.en: JOANNA: That's right.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 没错。

sentences.en: My research investigated the way players see their role as a musician and how this is linked to the type of clothing they decide to wear.
sentences.zh: 我的研究考察了演奏者如何看待自身作为音乐家的角色，以及这种角色认知如何影响其最终选择的演出服装类型。

sentences.en: But that focus didn't emerge immediately.
sentences.zh: 但这一研究焦点并非一开始就明确确立。

sentences.en: When I started I was more interested in & 26 trying to investigate the impact of what was worn on those listening, and also whether someone like a violinist might adopt a different style of clothing from, & 26 say, someone playing the flute or the trumpet.
sentences.zh: 最初，我更感兴趣的是探究演出服装对听众所产生的影响，同时也想了解小提琴手是否会像长笛或小号演奏者那样，采用不同风格的着装。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: It's interesting that the choice of dress is up to the individual, isn't it?
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 有趣的是，着装选择完全由个人决定，对吧？

sentences.en: JOANNA: Yes, you'd expect there to be rules about it in orchestras, but that's quite rare.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 是的，人们本以为交响乐团中会存在相关着装规定，但实际上这种情况相当罕见。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: You only had women performers in your study.
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 你的研究中只纳入了女性表演者。

sentences.en: Was that because male musicians are less worried about fashion?
sentences.zh: 这是否是因为男性音乐家对时尚的关注度较低？

sentences.en: JOANNA: think a lot of the men are very much influenced by fashion, but in social terms the choices they have are more limited…... they'd really upset audiences if they strayed away from quite narrow boundaries.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 我认为许多男性音乐家其实深受时尚影响，但从社会层面来看，他们可选择的着装范围却更为有限……一旦突破某些相当狭窄的界限，就很可能令观众感到不适。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: Hmm.
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 嗯。

sentences.en: Now, popular music has quite different expectations.
sentences.zh: 流行音乐领域则有着截然不同的着装期待。

sentences.en: Did you read Mike Frost's article about the dress of women performers in popular music?
sentences.zh: 你读过迈克·弗罗斯特关于流行音乐女性表演者着装的文章吗？

sentences.en: JOANNA: No.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 没有。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: He points out that a lot of female singers and musicians in popular music tend to dress down in performances, and wear less feminine clothes, like jeans instead of skirts, and he suggests this is because otherwise they'd just be discounted as 028 trivial.
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 他指出，流行音乐中大量女性歌手及乐手在演出时倾向于‘低调着装’，即穿着偏中性化的服装，例如用牛仔裤代替裙子；他推测，这是因为若不如此，她们便容易被简单视为肤浅、无足轻重。

sentences.en: JOANNA: But you could argue they're just wearing what's practical ...
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 但你也可以说，她们只是选择了更实用的服装……

sentences.en: I mean, a pop-music concert is usually a pretty energetic affair.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一场流行音乐会通常是一场相当充满活力的演出。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: Yes, he doesn't make that point, but I think you're probably right. was interested by the effect of the audience at a musical performance when it came to the choice of dress.
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 是的，他并未提及这一点，但我认为你的观点很可能是正确的。我对观众在音乐表演中对演出者着装选择所产生的影响特别感兴趣。

sentences.en: JOANNA: The subjects I interviewed felt this was really important.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 我所访谈的受试者普遍认为这一点确实至关重要。

sentences.en: It's all to do with what we understand by a performance as a public event.
sentences.zh: 这与我们对‘演出’作为一种公共事件的理解密切相关。

sentences.en: They believed the audience had certain expectations and it was up to them as performers to fulfil these expectations, to show a kind of esteem
sentences.zh: 她们相信观众怀有特定的期待，而作为表演者，她们有责任满足这些期待，以此展现某种尊重与敬意。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: ...
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: ...

sentences.en: they weren't afraid of looking as if they'd made an effort to look good.
sentences.zh: 她们并不担心看起来像是刻意打扮过、力求外表出众。

sentences.en: JOANNA: Mmm. think in the past the audience would have had those expectations of one another too, but that's not really the case now, not in the UK anyway.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 嗯。我觉得过去观众彼此之间也会有这类期待，但如今情况已大不相同，至少在英国是这样。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: No.
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 不是的。

sentences.en: JOANNA: And also got interested in what sports scientists are doing too, with regard to clothing.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 同时，我也开始关注运动科学家在服装领域所开展的研究工作。

sentences.en: Audioscripts
sentences.zh: 听力原文

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: Musicians are quite vulnerable physically, aren't they, because the movements they carry out are very intensive and repetitive, so I'd imagine some features of sports clothing could safeguard the players from the potentially dangerous.
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 音乐家在身体上其实相当脆弱，对吧？因为他们所进行的动作强度高且高度重复，所以我猜想运动服的某些特性或许能保护演奏者，使其免受此类潜在危险的影响。

sentences.en: effects of this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 这类情况可能带来的影响。

sentences.en: JOANNA: Yes, but musicians don't really consider it.
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 是的，但音乐家实际上并未对此加以考虑。

sentences.en: They avoid clothing that obviously restricts their movements, but that's as far as they go.
sentences.zh: 他们只会避开那些明显限制自身活动的服装，仅此而已。

sentences.en: SUPERVISOR: Anyway, coming back to your own research, do you have any idea where you're going from here?
sentences.zh: SUPERVISOR: 好吧，回到你自己的研究上来——你接下来打算朝哪个方向推进呢？

sentences.en: JOANNA: I was thinking of doing a study using an audience, including ...
sentences.zh: JOANNA: 我正考虑开展一项面向观众的研究，包括……
